paite: Huai ni in Deborah leh Abinoam tapa Barak in hiai la asa uhi:
heading: Debora Leh Barak La
english: Then Deborah and Barak the son of Abinoam sang on that day, saying,

paite: "Israel a makaite'n ma akaih lai un, amau ut thu a mite'n azuih lai un, TOUPA phat un!
english: “Because the leaders took the lead in Israel, because the people offered themselves willingly, be blessed, Yahweh!

paite: Aw, nou kumpipate aw, ngaikhia un. Aw, nou heutute aw, bil na doh un. Kei mahmah in TOUPA pahtawi in la ka sa dia, TOUPA, Israelte' Pathian phat in la ka sa ding hi.
english: “Hear, you kings! Give ear, you princes! I, even I, will sing to Yahweh. I will sing praise to Yahweh, the God of Israel.

paite: TOUPA, Seir gam a pan na hong paikhiak a, Edom loubuk a na hong pawt in, lei aling a, van ahong kia a, meipi'n vuah azusak uhi.
english: “Yahweh, when you went out of Seir, when you marched out of the field of Edom, the earth trembled, the sky also dropped. Yes, the clouds dropped water.

paite: TOUPA ma ah tangte achim ua, TOUPA, Israelte' Pathian ma ah Sinai Tang mah leng.
english: The mountains quaked at Yahweh’s presence, even Sinai at the presence of Yahweh, the God of Israel.

paite: Anath tapa Samgar dam lai nite leh Jael dam lai nite in lamliante tot louh in a-om ua, zin-le-lengte lah lam neute ah apai uhi.
english: “In the days of Shamgar the son of Anath, in the days of Jael, the highways were unoccupied. The travelers walked through byways.

paite: Israel gamte atul khin a, akhuate luah louh in atul khin hi, kei Deborah ka gamtang a, Israel gam nu ka gamtat masiah.
english: The rulers ceased in Israel. They ceased until I, Deborah, arose; Until I arose a mother in Israel.

paite: Amau pathian thakte atel ua; huchi in kulh kongkhak bul ah kidouna a-om a; Israel gam a mi singli lak ah lum leh tei muh in a-om hia?
english: They chose new gods. Then war was in the gates. Was there a shield or spear seen among forty thousand in Israel?

paite: Ka lungsim Israelte vaihawmpa, mipite lak a lungluttak a kipiate lam ah a-om hi. TOUPA phat un.
english: My heart is toward the governors of Israel, who offered themselves willingly among the people. Bless Yahweh!

paite: Pau un, nou sabiltung kang tung a tuangte, nou vaihawmna a tute leh lampi a paite.
english: “Speak, you who ride on white donkeys, you who sit on rich carpets, and you who walk by the way.

paite: Thalkap mite husa zak phak louh, tui tawina mun ah TOUPA thil dik hihte agengen ua, Israel gam tung a thil dik ahihte ngei. Huchi in TOUPA mipite kulh kongkhakte lam ah apaisuk ding uhi.
english: Far from the noise of archers, in the places of drawing water, there they will rehearse Yahweh’s righteous acts, the righteous acts of his rule in Israel. “Then Yahweh’s people went down to the gates.

paite: Thou in, thou in, Deborah; thou in, thou in, la sa in. Thou in, Barak, thou inla, Abinoam tapa, na salmatte pi in.
english: ‘Awake, awake, Deborah! Awake, awake, utter a song! Arise, Barak, and lead away your captives, you son of Abinoam.’

paite: Huchi in mi omlaite mipite lak a miliante tung ah thu aneisak a, TOUPA'N mihat tung ah thu hon neisak hi.
english: “Then a remnant of the nobles and the people came down. Yahweh came down for me against the mighty.

paite: Ephraim a pan zungzam khat Amalek dou a-om a, Benjamin, na mite lak a mite'n nang hon zui uh, Makir a pan gam vaihawmte ahong paisuk ua, Zebulun a pan laigelhmi chiangkhun tawi mite ahong paisuk uhi.
english: Those whose root is in Amalek came out of Ephraim, after you, Benjamin, among your peoples. Governors come down out of Machir. Those who handle the marshal’s staff came out of Zebulun.

paite: Deborah kiang ah Issakar miliante a-om ua; Issakar leh Barak mah leng. Amah phaizang lam a sawlsuk ahi a, Reuben pawlte ahihleh nakpitak in akingaihtuah lai uhi.
english: The princes of Issachar were with Deborah. As was Issachar, so was Barak. They rushed into the valley at his feet. By the watercourses of Reuben, there were great resolves of heart.

paite: Bangziak a belam huang lak a tu nilouh, belamhon ham ngai ding lel in maw? Reuben pawlte a ding in lungtang a kingaihtuahna thupitak a-om hi.
english: Why did you sit among the sheepfolds? To hear the whistling for the flocks? At the watercourses of Reuben, there were great searchings of heart.

paite: Gileadte Jordan gal ah a-om nilouh ua; bangziak a Dante longte a om nilouh uh ahia? Asherte tuipi piau ah atu kinken ua, atuipiaute ah a-om nilouh uhi.
english: Gilead lived beyond the Jordan. Why did Dan remain in ships? Asher sat still at the haven of the sea, and lived by his creeks.

paite: Zebulun leh Naphtali leng mun sang pawn a sih ngap gigete ahi uh.
english: Zebulun was a people that jeopardized their lives to the death; Naphtali also, on the high places of the field.

paite: Kumpipate'n ahong dou ua, Kanaan kumpipate'n Meggiddo tui kiang, Taanak ah adou ua; sum himhim ala kei uhi.
english: “The kings came and fought, then the kings of Canaan fought at Taanach by the waters of Megiddo. They took no plunder of silver.

paite: Van a pan ahon dou ua; aksite'n amun ua kipan Sisera ahon dou uh.
english: From the sky the stars fought. From their courses, they fought against Sisera.

paite: Kishon lui in amaute ataimang a, nidanglai lui, Kishon lui in, Aw ka kha, hattak in pai zel in.
english: The river Kishon swept them away, that ancient river, the river Kishon. My soul, march on with strength.

paite: Huchi in sakolte akipek thotthot ua, sakol hatte atawmtawm ziak un.
english: Then the horse hoofs stamped because of the prancing, the prancing of their strong ones.

paite: Meroz hamsiat un," TOUPA angel in achi, huai a tengte nakpitak in hamsiat un. TOUPA panpih ding, TOUPA'N mihattak adouna panpih dia ahong louh ziak un.
english: ‘Curse Meroz,’ said Yahweh’s angel. ‘Curse bitterly its inhabitants, because they didn’t come to help Yahweh, to help Yahweh against the mighty.’

paite: Numei lak ah Jael, Ken mi Heber zi nuamsapen ahi, numei puanin a tengte lak ah amah minuamsapen ahi.
english: “Jael shall be blessed above women, the wife of Heber the Kenite; blessed shall she be above women in the tent.

paite: Tui ahong ngen a, ama'n nawitui apia hi: miliante' nou in nawituidat ana pia hi.
english: He asked for water. She gave him milk. She brought him butter in a lordly dish.

paite: Kilhna atawi a, ataklam in nasemmi sek; sek in Sisera akhen a, alu ah akhen pailet a, ahi, ahaizek ah akhen a, akhental vengvong hi.
english: She put her hand to the tent peg, and her right hand to the workmen’s hammer. With the hammer she struck Sisera. She struck through his head. Yes, she pierced and struck through his temples.

paite: Akhebul ah akun a, apuk a, alum a; akhebul ah akun a, apukta a; apukna mun ah asita hi.
english: At her feet he bowed, he fell, he lay. At her feet he bowed, he fell. Where he bowed, there he fell down dead.

paite: Sisera nu bel tawlet ah adak a, vathangkalh awng ah asam a, "Bang achia kangtalai hong tunghak ahia? Bang achia akangtalai khe zekai ahia?" achi hi.
english: “Through the window she looked out, and cried: Sisera’s mother looked through the lattice. ‘Why is his chariot so long in coming? Why do the wheels of his chariots wait?’

paite: Anumei pilte'n ana dawng ua, ahi, amah dawng ding in ahong nawn ua:
english: Her wise ladies answered her, Yes, she returned answer to herself,

paite: Amuzouta kei ua hia? Gallak kihawmta lou uhia? Michih in nungak khat hiam nih chiat; Sisera tan ding gallak puan ze tuamtuam, gallak puan ze kilawm, ze tuamtuam, gallak ngawng a velh ding puan, alangnih a ze kilawm, ze tuamtuam, chi in.
english: ‘Have they not found, have they not divided the plunder? A lady, two ladies to every man; to Sisera a plunder of dyed garments, a plunder of dyed garments embroidered, of dyed garments embroidered on both sides, on the necks of the plunder?’

paite: "Huchibang in aw, TOUPA, na melmate tengteng mangthang vek uhen. Amah itte bel hattak a pai, nisa bang hi uhen,” achi uhi. Huchi in kum sawmli sung gam galmuang in a-om hi.
english: “So let all your enemies perish, Yahweh, but let those who love him be as the sun when it rises in its strength.” Then the land had rest forty years.
